question: Which statement best describes The iterable protocol (Symbol.iterator)?
options: for...of, the spread operator `[...x]`, array/parameter destructuring, `Array.from`, `Promise.all`, and Map/Set constructors all consume iterables by calling Symbol.iterator and looping until done. Making something iterable means it works everywhere these consumers are used — no special-casing required.

An object is iterable if it has a method keyed by the well-known symbol `Symbol.iterator` that returns an iterator. Arrays, strings, Maps, Sets, and arguments are all built-in iterables. Implementing this one method lets your own objects work with for...of, spread, and destructuring.

A generator function (declared with `function*`) returns a generator object that is both an iterator AND iterable. Each `yield` pauses execution and emits a value; calling next() resumes from exactly where it left off, preserving all local state. This makes writing iterators dramatically simpler than hand-rolling next().

An iterator is any object with a `next()` method that returns `{ value, done }`. `done` is false while values remain and true when the sequence is exhausted; `value` carries the current item (and, on the final result, an optional return value). Consumers call next() repeatedly until done is true.
